question: Should the RFC-defined Claw lifecycle ownership model become an experiment-gated core Doctor surface once the prerequisite ownership stack is accepted?
rationale: This adds a new persistent-state diagnostic capability to core, and the existing experiment gate does not establish long-term ownership, support expectations, or upgrade policy.

options.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics direction
options.body: Accept the experiment-gated core surface after the stacked ownership contract lands, the concurrent read safety is repaired, and real behavior proof is supplied.

options.title: Defer with the RFC stack
options.body: Keep this PR and its dependent work open but unlanded until maintainers evaluate the full Claws ownership and update workflow together.

options.title: Decline the core lifecycle surface
options.body: Close the stack if lifecycle ownership and reconciliation should not become a supported OpenClaw core capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics direction
recommendation.body: Accept the experiment-gated core surface after the stacked ownership contract lands, the concurrent read safety is repaired, and real behavior proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of shared SQLite and Doctor safeguards makes this the best available decision route for the persistent-state and core-product boundary.
